_: Which files go into the package `tools/mac-logic-tests` builds, and why the rest do not.
Every .swift file under a `watched` directory has to be in `in` or in `out` (with `why`) of `sources` or `tests`;
one that is in neither makes the script fail and name it. Files from elsewhere may be listed in `sources.in` when a test needs them.
An entry is a path, or an object: `path`, and to take only part of a file `from` / `until` (each a string found on exactly one line;
`from` is the first line taken, `until` the first line not taken), `drop` (whole lines to remove), `prepend` (lines to put first).
A part is copied, not linked; a marker that is no longer there is a failure. Say with `why` what a part or an exclusion costs.
`objc` are Objective-C files (.h and .m) the Swift calls through the app's bridging header; they are built as a target of their own
and every .h among them is imported into the Swift the way the bridging header imports it.
